cards.back: Pumps blood throughout the body via the circulatory system. Beats ~100,000 times per day.
Exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide during respiration. Contain ~300 million alveoli.
Central organ of the nervous system. Controls thought, memory, emotion, movement, and organ function.
Largest internal organ. Detoxifies chemicals, metabolizes drugs, produces bile, and stores glycogen.
Filter blood to produce urine, removing waste and regulating fluid balance, electrolytes, and blood pressure.
Breaks down food using hydrochloric acid and enzymes (pepsin). Holds 1–1.5 liters of food.
Primary site of nutrient absorption. ~20 feet long with villi that increase surface area.
Absorbs water and electrolytes from remaining food matter. Houses gut microbiome bacteria.
Produces insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar. Also secretes digestive enzymes into the small intestine.
Filters blood, removing old red blood cells. Stores white blood cells and platelets for immune defense.
Largest organ by area. Protects against pathogens, regulates temperature, and provides sensory reception.
206 bones in adults. Provides structure, protects organs, enables movement, and produces blood cells in marrow.
Over 600 muscles. Three types: skeletal (voluntary), smooth (involuntary), and cardiac (heart).
Heart, blood vessels, and blood. Delivers oxygen/nutrients to cells and removes waste products.
Nose, trachea, bronchi, lungs. Facilitates gas exchange: O₂ in, CO₂ out.
Brain, spinal cord, and nerves. Central (CNS) and peripheral (PNS) divisions. Transmits electrical signals.
Glands that produce hormones: thyroid, adrenal, pituitary, pancreas. Regulates metabolism, growth, and reproduction.
Defends against pathogens. Includes white blood cells, antibodies, lymph nodes, thymus, and spleen.
Mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine. Breaks down food and absorbs nutrients.
Kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra. Filters blood waste into urine, maintains fluid and electrolyte balance.
Network of lymph vessels and nodes. Drains excess tissue fluid, transports immune cells, and filters pathogens.
Butterfly-shaped gland in the neck. Produces T3 and T4 hormones that regulate metabolism and energy.
Sit atop each kidney. Produce cortisol (stress), aldosterone (blood pressure), and adrenaline (fight-or-flight).
"Master gland" at brain base. Produces growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, and controls other endocrine glands.
Carry oxygen via hemoglobin. No nucleus. ~70% of body's iron. Live ~120 days.
Fight infection. Types: neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils.
Cell fragments that form blood clots to stop bleeding. Normal count: 150,000–400,000 per microliter.
Thighbone — the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
Dome-shaped muscle below the lungs. Contracts during inhalation to draw air into the lungs.
Located at the back of the brain. Coordinates voluntary movements, balance, and motor learning.
Part of the limbic system. Critical for forming new memories and spatial navigation.
Soft tissue inside bones. Red marrow produces blood cells; yellow marrow stores fat.
Stores and concentrates bile produced by the liver. Releases bile to help digest fats.
Small pouch attached to the large intestine. May serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria.
Muscular tube (~25 cm) connecting the throat to the stomach. Moves food via peristalsis.
